parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file sits in the infrastructure layer, and everything it does is persistence work, which is the job of that layer. ProductRepository keeps Product aggregates in an in-memory Map and has only storage methods: save, findById, findAll, delete and exists. It has no business rules, no validation, no orchestration that would belong in the application layer, and no transport or presentation logic. Using the NestJS @Injectable decorator is framework wiring, which is also fine in infrastructure. The application handlers inject the concrete repository rather than a port, but that is a dependency-direction concern and out of scope for this rule.
